title: build(deps): resolve open dependabot advisories
description:
## Summary

Clears 15 of the 16 open Dependabot alerts on `main`. All of them are transitive — no direct dependency of this service is itself vulnerable — so the fix is a lockfile lift plus one direct bump where a parent pins the vulnerable version exactly.

**`find-my-way`** was pinned to `9.6.0` by `@nestjs/platform-fastify@11.1.28`. Bumping that dependency to `11.1.29` pulls in `find-my-way@9.7.0` and also aligns it with `@nestjs/common`/`@nestjs/core`, which are already on `11.1.29`. As a side effect the peer requirement on `@fastify/static` improves: `11.1.29` requests `^10.1.2`, which the project's `10.1.3` satisfies (`11.1.28` requested `^8 || ^9`, which it did not).

Everything else resolved inside the existing semver ranges via `yarn up -R`. `@nestjs/platform-fastify@11.2.x` and `find-my-way@9.8.0` were left alone as too young for the 7-day `npmMinimalAgeGate` in `.yarnrc.yml`; `9.7.0` is above the advisory's `<=9.6.0` vulnerable range, so it is sufficient.

**One alert is deliberately left open:** the `js-yaml` 5.x DoS advisory (`>=5.0.0 <=5.2.1`, high). `@nestjs/swagger@11.4.6` pins `js-yaml@5.2.1` exactly, and `11.4.7` already ships the fix upstream (it pins `5.3.0`) — it is just younger than the age gate right now. Rather than carry a `resolutions` entry that would have to be removed again, this clears on the next `@nestjs/swagger` bump.

`yarn npm audit --all --recursive` reports no other security advisories. The three remaining entries it prints are npm *deprecation* notices, not advisories, and all are dev-only transitives with no fixed version available: `@sinonjs/text-encoding` and `lodash.get` (via `aws-sdk-client-mock` → `sinon`) and `cron-parser@4` (via `bullmq`).

Verified with `yarn format`, `yarn lint`, `yarn build`, and `yarn test` (348 files, 6169 tests passing).

## Changes

- `package.json` — bump `@nestjs/platform-fastify` `11.1.28` → `11.1.29`
- `yarn.lock` — patched transitives: `brace-expansion` `1.1.16` → `1.1.18` and `5.0.7` → `5.0.9`, `fast-uri` `3.1.4` → `3.1.5`, `find-my-way` `9.6.0` → `9.7.0`, `js-yaml` `4.3.0` → `4.3.1`, `nanoid` `3.3.12` → `3.3.18`, `postcss` `8.5.15`/`8.5.19` → `8.5.26`, `tar` `7.5.20` → `7.5.22`, `undici` `8.7.0` → `8.10.0`

findings.claim: js-yaml@5.2.1 is still resolved in the lockfile even though the PR's goal is to clear the open advisories; it is pinned exactly by the production dependency @nestjs/swagger@11.4.6 (package.json:63), so the known js-yaml advisory remains in the production dependency tree after this change. Bumping @nestjs/swagger to 11.4.7 would resolve it, and is preferable to adding a resolutions override that fights the exact pin.

The commit body's phrase 'lift the transitive resolutions' could be misread as adding Yarn resolutions entries, when in fact no resolutions were added and the upgrades are lockfile-only changes within existing semver ranges; if this text is reused as the PR body, wording such as 're-resolve transitive dependencies in yarn.lock' would state it more clearly.

The dependency @nestjs/serve-static 5.0.5 still declares a peer range of ^8.0.4 || ^9.0.0 for @fastify/static, which the installed @fastify/static 10.1.3 does not satisfy; since ServeStaticModule is used in src/app.module.ts, this pre-existing peer mismatch remains unresolved, though it was not introduced by this PR.

The find-my-way bump from 9.6.0 to 9.7.0 restructures its core matching loop (a new while(true) in find, isParamSafe flipped, and a fallback for optional params), which changes routing behavior for every endpoint alongside the app's ignoreTrailingSlash and maxParamLength settings (src/app.provider.ts:36-46). Since no tests, install, or build were run as part of the review, this routing change has not been verified and could introduce a regression that only CI would catch.

@fastify/cookie is pinned with a caret range (^11.1.1) instead of an exact version, which is an exception to the convention that runtime dependencies be pinned exactly; it is unchanged by this diff but could be addressed as a follow-up.

@fastify/static is pinned with a caret range (^10.1.3) instead of an exact version, which is an exception to the convention that runtime dependencies be pinned exactly; it is unchanged by this diff but could be addressed as a follow-up.
